text:
maria: heads up — after the 03:00 UTC deploy we started seeing a pattern of grpc streaming sessions dropping from ap-northeast-1 (tokyo). lots of RST_STREAM/CANCEL and clients reconnecting repeatedly.

sre-bot: [ALERT] 03:12:22 - increased grpc_stream_resets (5xx) :: service=chat-inference region=ap-northeast-1 count=143 in 5m

kevin: any obvious config changes in this deploy? envoy or lb?

maria: only the model-serving side rolled (small infra change) — no explicit envoy changes. attaching a sample from the pod logs: 
```
[2026-03-17T03:09:41Z] envoy [warning] stream id=0 RST_STREAM: CANCEL, upstream: 10.3.12.45:8080, downstream: 172.20.1.14:43122
[2026-03-17T03:09:41Z] grpc: stream error: code = Internal desc = stream terminated by RST_STREAM
[2026-03-17T03:09:41Z] connection: http2: server sent GOAWAY, lastStreamID=15, ErrCode=NO_ERROR
```

ada: quick hypothesis: NAT ephemeral port exhaustion + HTTP/2 connection reuse. clients keep long-lived upstream connections but SNAT port pool on the node/NAT gateway is rotating, so some backend connections see source port changes and proxy/edge closes streams. seen similar behavior when ephemeral port ranges are small or concurrency is huge.

leo: interesting — any metrics evidence? tcp_established / ephemeral ports used?

maria: running a quick check on a problem node: `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range` -> `32768 60999`
`ss -tn sport = :443 | wc -l` -> 64000+ sockets during the spike (node level).

kevin: that looks close to the range limit. if each upstream connection consumes a source port and we do aggressive connection pooling per pod, we can exhaust. that explains GOAWAY + RST when the kernel reuses ports.

ada: mitigation options (short-term):
- widen ip_local_port_range on nodes to give more ephemeral ports
- enable per-node SNAT (assign EIPs) to increase available mappings
- reduce connection churn by increasing http2 max_concurrent_streams (fewer physical tcp connections)
- add HTTP/2 PING keepalive to detect stale connections earlier

maria: suggestion: do ephemeral range + envoy config tweak first, then monitor. widening range is quick but not permanent.

kevin: I can push a daemonset to set `sysctl.net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = "15000 65000"` and bump `tcp_tw_reuse` on the nodes. will also add an env var to the serving pods to reduce connection pools: `GRPC_MAX_CONNECTIONS=20`.

leo: for envoy we should also set `max_connection_duration` and `drain_timeout` to avoid long-lived zombie conns. i'd propose `max_connection_duration: 1h` and `connection_keepalive: 30s` for now.

maria: opened JIRA INC-2248 with logs + tentative plan: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INC-2248

ada: one more data point — cloud NAT (ap-northeast) shows high SNAT utilization for the VPC (dashboard: /dashboards/nat-util). if APAC traffic keeps growing we'll need a more durable plan (static EIPs or per-node source NAT pools) instead of just widening ports.

kevin: agreed — short-term changes deployed. i'll coordinate with infra to get EIP pool request if we keep seeing >80% SNAT usage.

maria: deployed sysctl daemonset to canaries at 03:28 UTC, envoy config bump to `max_concurrent_streams=256` on canaries at 03:35. monitoring now.

sre-bot: [INFO] 03:40:00 - canary nodes ephemeral ports widened, envoy config applied to 2/2 canaries

leo: please watch for increased TIME_WAIT count — widening range helps but if we don't reduce tcp churn it will just shift the problem. long-term: connection multiplexing + smarter egress routing (per-az NAT pools) + client backpressure.

maria: noted. i'll add alert for `nat_snat_utilization > 75%` and `grpc_resets_rate > 3/min` for ap-northeast-1. tagging @kevin for follow-up. :pray:

kevin: will follow up with infra team re: EIPs and we should consider a small perf test to measure per-connection port usage for grpc workloads.

ada: also leaving a note — check envoy version for the known http2 GOAWAY bug in 1.26 where PING frames weren't handled consistently under SNAT churn. if we can bump to 1.30 in next maintenance window that reduces RST noise.

maria: thanks all. i'll post updates in this thread and close INC-2248 when stable. :white_check_mark:
